data.body:
Closing evidence. Change 2976 carried LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and has merged; origin/main is now e46d03aa83c, and the landed tree contains both the `cat >/dev/null` drain and the new oracle `test_credential_stub_drains_stdin_so_writer_cannot_take_sigpipe`.

Acceptance criteria, item by item:

1. The fake credential helper consumes the credential request before returning — met. The stub's `credential)` arm now runs `cat >/dev/null` before emitting its response, matching real `git credential fill`, which always drains its request. Because the arm stays alive until the writer closes the pipe, the writer can no longer lose the race.

2. A deterministic regression oracle covers the pipefail/SIGPIPE failure class — met, and validated in both directions rather than merely added. The oracle delays the writer past the point where a non-draining stub would already have exited, which converts the scheduling race into a fixed outcome. Removing the drain makes it fail on every run with returncode 141, which is 128 + SIGPIPE; restoring the drain makes it pass on every run. That two-sided check is what distinguishes an oracle from another racy test, and it matters here: in the very run where the oracle failed against the unfixed stub, the pre-existing test passed. The pre-existing test is itself the race, so it could never have served as its own regression guard.

3. The focused feature-branch inventory tests pass under the CI shell environment — met. Locally the file was run 20 consecutive times with 2 passed each run, 40 passes and 0 failures. Authoritatively, CI ran the suite on the patchset and returned Verified +1 (GitHub Actions run 35173352827), which is the Linux/Bash environment this criterion names.

4. Gerrit LLM-Review and Verified pass before merge — met. Both labels were +1 on patch set 1 before submit, and the change was not WIP.

Implementation note beyond the plan: the stub was extracted into a shared `_git_stub(calls)` helper so the oracle and the original test read from one definition. Without that the oracle would guard a copy of the stub rather than the stub actually used by the test it protects, and the two could drift apart silently.

One process finding surfaced while closing this ticket and is being filed separately: the MCP server's code workspace (docker volume `gerrit_mcp_code`) is cloned once by the MCP entrypoint and never refreshed, so it had frozen at 2026-09-07 and was 130 commits behind origin/main. Every completion-verification and plan-review gate reads that tree, so gates were verifying stale code. It was fast-forwarded to the current tip so this ticket and the preceding one could be verified against the real tree.
